item.html:
Expert Commercial Roof Installation & Replacement

A commercial roof is one of the most critical structural components and largest capital investments for any business facility. When repairs are no longer cost-effective, or when severe Texas storms have compromised your building's envelope, a full commercial roof replacement becomes a necessity. Unlike residential roofing, commercial replacements require advanced engineering to manage large-scale drainage, heavy rooftop HVAC equipment, and strict local building codes.

At Core Four Roofing, our commercial installation process is built around safety, precision, and business continuity. Whether we are conducting a complete tear-off of an aging modified bitumen system or installing a brand new, highly reflective TPO membrane on a new construction project, we handle every detail. From replacing compromised decking and upgrading insulation to ensuring watertight seals around all roof penetrations, we deliver a long-lasting roofing system designed to protect your tenants and your bottom line for decades.

item.html: Frequently Asked Questions About Commercial Replacements
item.text: Frequently Asked Questions About Commercial Replacements

items.q: Can you install a new commercial roof over my existing one?
items.a: In some cases, yes. This is called a "roof overlay" or "recover." If your existing roof has only one layer, the underlying insulation is dry, and the deck is structurally sound, building codes may allow us to install a new membrane directly over the old one, saving you significant tear-off costs.

items.q: How long does a full commercial roof replacement take?
items.a: The timeline depends entirely on the size of the facility, the type of material being installed, and weather conditions. However, because we deploy large, experienced commercial crews and stage our materials efficiently, we can complete massive flat roof replacements much faster than industry averages, keeping you fully informed at every phase.

items.q: What is the best roofing material for a commercial building in Texas?
items.a: TPO (Thermoplastic Polyolefin) is currently the most popular choice for Texas flat roofs due to its brilliant white, heat-reflective surface and cost-effectiveness. However, we also highly recommend PVC for facilities exposed to chemicals or grease, and metal for sloped commercial buildings.

items.q: Do you help with commercial roof insurance claims?
items.a: Absolutely. If your commercial roof replacement is necessary due to severe hail, wind, or hurricane damage, our team provides comprehensive, code-compliant damage reports and will work directly with your insurance adjuster to ensure your property is fully restored.
